project_description: The project addresses substantial physical barriers that currently limit equitable access to behavioral health services at 905 Washington Street. Although portions of the building were renovated to support psychiatric and MAT treatment services, the facility currently lacks a fully ADA-compliant accessible route from designated parking areas into the treatment environment. Individuals with mobility limitations, chronic medical conditions, or physical disabilities face unnecessary barriers to independently accessing behavioral health treatment services. Program funding will support construction of an ADA-accessible route from designated handicapped parking spaces to the treatment facility through installation of a compliant exterior ramp system leading to an elevated deck area and direct building entry. The project also addresses a significant interior life-safety and patient access issue affecting second-floor clinical space currently utilized for behavioral health treatment. The existing interior stair system limits safe and efficient access to second-floor treatment areas due to inadequate pitch and spatial limitations. This creates challenges for patients, staff, and individuals with mobility concerns seeking behavioral health services upstairs. The project also addresses infrastructure conditions that threaten the long-term viability of behavioral health treatment space at the 905 Washington Street facility. Roof deterioration and water intrusion have affected portions of the building, including areas supporting existing behavioral health services. Without intervention, continued deterioration risks progressive damage to treatment space, increased maintenance costs, and potential reduction in usable licensed service capacity.

project_description: IUP will address the critical shortage of healthcare providers in the Appalachian region and other rural regions of the Commonwealth. The goal is to implement a comprehensive, statewide rural health workforce development model focused primarily on training primary care physicians to serve rural Pennsylvania, while collaborating closely with nursing and allied rural health professional training. This initiative will expand access to rural medical education, strengthen rural healthcare infrastructure, and improve long-term health outcomes for rural regions of the Commonwealth. By achieving a measurable increase in the percentage of Pennsylvania medical school graduates practicing in rural Pennsylvania, increasing the number of medical school students participating in rural clinical rotations and pursuing rural practice careers, expanding enrollment of rural and firstgeneration students entering rural medical education pathways, reducing average medical student debt levels relative to national benchmarks, and achieving measurable growth in public awareness and engagement of rural health career pathways, the Commonwealth will improve rural workforce placement and recruitment, improve health outcomes, and strengthen healthcare systems.

project_description: Through the RHTP, the University of Pittsburgh will establish and operate Regional Training Centers in partnership with Federally Qualified Health Centers and rural hospitals. The Regional Training Center model is a multidisciplinary educational and patient care initiative designed to address dental workforce shortages and improve rural oral health. The Regional Training Centers will provide training opportunities through a hybrid dental hygiene program, a hybrid dental assistant training program, and a General Practice Residency Program for recent dental school graduates. The project is intended to increase immediate access to dental care, create healthcare workforce opportunities for students from rural communities, and improve long-term access to care by increasing the number of trained providers who remain in the regions where they complete their education and training.

project_description: The Guthrie Clinic will pilot a centralized digital monitoring and support model to improve care coordination, ease staff workload, and achieve reductions in nurse turnover and hospital costs for the benefit of inpatient providers located within the Commonwealth’s RHTP rural-eligible area. The goal of the Pilot Program is to reduce avoidable patient safety events, improve response time to clinical needs, alleviate bedside nursing workload, and enhance the patient and caregiver experience at Pilot Locations. The Pilot Program is a transformative and innovative care delivery model that leverages highly trained, virtual healthcare professionals to provider 24/7 clinical support through in-room cameras and microphones. The parties anticipate the model will demonstrate effectiveness in reducing falls that result in major injury, decreasing administrative discharge times, decreasing length in stays, decreasing excess stays, and reducing bedside workload.
